entries.d6fe2efa7f50fffb: These are [[term:wafer|silicon wafers]], which serve as the “substrates” of semiconductors. They are made by growing a large silicon crystal about 30 centimeters in diameter from high-purity polycrystalline silicon as the raw material, then slicing it thin. The finished wafers are delivered to companies that make semiconductor devices (device makers), where they become semiconductors used in smartphones, personal computers, automobiles and other products.

It is highly durable and is used in water and sewer pipes, window frames, flooring materials, plastic wrap film, and other products. It is also made at the factories of its U.S. subsidiary Shintech INC. and the Netherlands' Shin-Etsu PVC B.V.
entries.e9c8cfc89a1684a8: This is a light-reactive resin used in the process of drawing circuit patterns on silicon wafers for semiconductors and other devices. It is applied to the wafer surface, and circuit patterns are formed by exposing it to light through a photomask on which the circuit pattern is drawn.
